Description: Brainstormed, planned, and implemented Live Transcript Mode — a new skill that captures group discussion from a live Notion transcript during video calls and synthesizes it into an answer. Installed Notion MCP server globally for testing.

Tested live-transcript skill end-to-end against real Notion transcripts. Discovered transcript content lives inside meeting-notes blocks, not as page siblings — rewrote the skill from toggle-marker approach to subagent anchor-based extraction that protects the main context window. Connected repo to bcal-brain and promoted the architecture pattern as a reusable lesson.

Diagnosed why live-transcript skill wasn't appearing after plugin install — the plugin updater compares version strings in plugin.json, not git SHAs. Bumped to 0.2.0, confirmed update flow works. Added a pre-commit hook to block skill changes without a version bump. Promoted the lesson to bcal-brain.

Fixed /doctor warning by moving invalid preCommit Claude hook to a native git pre-commit hook. Enhanced end-session-gracefully skill to fetch Proof review status via API and include pending review links in NEXT_SESSION.md. Bumped plugin to 0.3.0.

Fixed notify-proof Unicode rendering in Slack by adding a sanitization table and migrating from webhook to bot token. Created notify-pdf skill for uploading PDFs to Slack. Unified both skills on shared Slack bot credentials with a single setup guide.

Set up Slack bot credentials and tested notify-proof and notify-pdf end-to-end. Migrated notify-pdf to Slack's new three-step upload API after discovering files.upload was deprecated. Built apply-claude-md-best-practices skill with Wharton-informed UX. Added lesson compounding step to end-session-gracefully. Bumped to 0.5.0.

Formalized the NEXT_SESSION.md contract between end-session-gracefully and start-session with YAML frontmatter (session_name, model, context_pct, ended_at). Fixed write-to-diary to never gitignore DIARY.csv and check for legacy gitignore entries. Added three new best practices to apply-claude-md-best-practices: Wharton AI adoption principles, agent-native architecture, and prompts-as-installers.
